intro: Synchronize DSH configuration, model providers, plugin inventory and configuration, secrets, and MCP servers across devices; plugin code itself is never uploaded. Backends: Git, WebDAV, and S3-compatible storage.
sectionCrash: The settings page failed to render. Reopen settings; details are in the browser console.
overviewDesc: How this device compares with the remote store.
overviewEmpty: No sync data to show yet.
overviewNotConfiguredHint: No sync backend is configured yet. Open Config, choose Git, WebDAV, or S3-compatible storage, and save to start syncing.
overviewAutoSyncFailures: Automatic sync failed {count} time(s) in a row; check the connection in Config.
overviewSectionsDesc: Each section reports its own local and remote items, changes, and conflicts.
syncDesc: Preview a plan first and confirm before running; nothing is deleted or overwritten without confirmation.
directionHintPush: Upload this device’s state to the remote store.
directionHintPull: Overwrite this device with the remote store.
directionHintTwoWay: Upload local changes, then download remote changes.
syncNeedsPreview: Preview a plan before running it.
syncPushConflictBlocked: Backup (upload) cannot resolve conflicts one by one; resolve them first or use two-way sync.
syncConflictPrompt: Choose how to resolve every conflict before running.
syncConflictAllChosen: Every conflict has a choice; the plan can run.
planRequiresConfirm: The plan contains destructive steps and needs confirmation.
conflictEffectLocal: Local content replaces the remote copy; other devices receive it on their next sync.
conflictEffectRemote: Remote content replaces this device; local changes are lost.
conflictEffectSkip: Nothing changes for this item; the same conflict returns on the next sync.
conflictReasonBothChanged: Changed on both sides with different results
conflictReasonLocalDeleted: Removed here; the remote store still has it
conflictReasonRemoteDeleted: Removed remotely; it still exists here
confirmSyncDesc: The steps below will run; destructive steps delete or overwrite content.
confirmRollbackDesc: This device returns to that historical revision; later local changes are lost.
configDesc: Choose the sync backend and its scope. Secret values are read only from environment variables or local private configuration and never written into synchronized data.
configBackendHintGit: Store snapshots and history in a Git repository on any Git host.
configBackendHintWebdav: Store data in a WebDAV collection, for example Nextcloud.
configBackendHintS3: Store data in S3-compatible object storage, for example MinIO or R2.
configRepoUrlHint: Accepts https, ssh, scp-style, or a file:// path.
configAuthHelperHint: Use credentials supplied by the system Git credential manager.
configAuthSshHint: Use the system SSH agent or a key under ~/.ssh.
configAuthHttpsTokenHint: Read an access token from an environment variable over HTTPS.
configTokenEnvVarHint: Name of the environment variable holding the token; the page neither reads nor displays the token.
configUsernameHint: Leave empty to use the provider default.
configWebdavPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the password already stored on this device.
configWebdavTokenHint: Can replace the username and password; leave empty to keep the stored value.
configS3PrefixHint: Key prefix inside the bucket; leave empty for the bucket root.
configS3SecretHint: Leave empty to keep the value already stored on this device.
configS3SessionTokenHint: Needed for temporary credentials; leave empty to keep the stored value.
configS3ForcePathStyleHint: Most self-hosted gateways (MinIO and similar) require this.
configDeviceNameHint: Shown in sync status and history.
configProfilesHint: The profile this process runs in is always included.
configScopesDesc: A disabled section is neither uploaded nor downloaded.
configScopesSecretsHint: Secrets always leave this device encrypted; set the passphrase environment variable first.
configPassphraseEnvVar: Passphrase environment variable name (the name, not the passphrase)
configPassphraseEnvVarHint: Put the variable NAME here, e.g. DSH_SYNC_PASSPHRASE; the passphrase itself goes in ~/.dsh/.env, which DSH reads once at startup, so a change needs a restart.
configAutoDesc: Check and sync in the background under the conditions below; conflicts or destructive plans pause it automatically.
autoEnabledHint: Master switch; nothing runs automatically while it is off.
autoStartupHint: Run one automatic sync after DSH starts.
autoStartupDelayHint: Wait for DSH to finish booting; 15 seconds or more is recommended.
autoPluginChangeHint: Trigger a delayed sync after plugins change, to avoid frequent runs.
autoDebounceHint: How long to wait after a detected change before running.
autoSaveFailed: Could not save the automatic sync settings: {message}
autoBehaviorHint: An automatic run pauses on conflicts or destructive plans and waits for manual action.
pluginsDesc: Only plugin names, versions, origins, install specs, and enabled state are synchronized; plugin code and local directories are never uploaded or recreated remotely.
pluginsNoCodeNotice: Plugin code is not synced: a new device reinstalls from the install spec, and local-path plugins cannot be restored.
pluginsOfficialHidden: {count} DeepSeek built-in bundles are hidden (not post-installed plugins, never synchronized)
pluginsLoadFailed: Could not load the plugin inventory: {message}
pluginsEmpty: No third-party plugins are installed on this device.
pluginsFilterPlaceholder: Filter by name, ID, or origin
pluginsSpecDesc: Check whether an install spec can rebuild this plugin on another device; nothing is installed.
pluginsSpecFailed: Could not check the install spec: {message}
mcpDesc: Synchronize MCP connection definitions, transports, and install methods; header and environment values are secret material, so only their names are synchronized.
mcpEmpty: No MCP servers on this device.
secretsDesc: This page shows only whether secrets exist, never a secret value. Secrets are stored remotely as an encrypted envelope.
secretsLoadFailed: Could not load the secrets status: {message}
secretsStored: The remote store has an encrypted secret document
secretsNotStored: The remote store has no encrypted secrets yet
secretsPassphraseHint: Set the passphrase in the environment variable {name} to decrypt.
secretsEnvVarNotSet: No passphrase environment variable is configured
secretsUnlockDesc: Open the remote envelope with the passphrase to confirm it is correct; the passphrase is never stored.
secretsUnlockOk: The passphrase is correct; the envelope holds {count} reference(s).
secretsUnlockFail: The passphrase is wrong or the envelope cannot be opened.
secretsNoValueNotice: This page never displays, reads, or submits a secret value.
historyDesc: Revisions in the remote store; this device can be restored to any of them.
historyEmpty: No history yet; it appears after the first backup.
logsDesc: Recent log entries from this plugin; secrets in log messages are redacted.
opRestartRequired: Some changes need a DSH restart to take effect.
configPassphraseEnvVarInvalid: An environment variable name may only contain letters, digits and underscores, and cannot start with a digit; do not put the passphrase value here.
configPassphraseEnvVarNotSet: Environment variable {name} has no value yet: put the passphrase in ~/.dsh/.env (a line {name}='your passphrase') and restart DSH.
